items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — jumped straight from greeting into looking up the profile with no roadmap for the call
Never asked whether the 4th-floor destination has an elevator, despite it being the single biggest time variable on this move
Never asked how many boxes — customer explicitly said her move is mostly 'boxes of personal belongings', and the 4-hour estimate was built without a box count
Did not probe additional rooms (garage, storage unit, balcony, kitchen, bathroom) — only asked bedroom, second bedroom, and living room
No moving-stressor question ('anything you're particularly worried about?')
No No Worries Damage Coverage pitch — $2,000 coverage never mentioned, and no 60¢/lb baseline insurance explanation at all
No full 'no hidden fees' pitch (no credit card fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees) — only said trip fee doesn't apply
Disassembly/reassembly included was never mentioned, even though the customer is moving a standing desk and two monitors
Packing service priced only as a vague 'extra time consideration' — no hourly rate or materials cost given
Never explained that the clock starts on-site when the contract opens
Stairs/elevator was never explained as an estimate variable (2nd floor origin, 4th floor destination)
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — no 'prep = shorter move = lower bill', no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip
Did not mention the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email or ask her to reply with corrections
Gave 'call us back' but never stated business hours
Never used the customer's name once in the whole call — used 'ma'am' instead, and openly admitted he couldn't remember how she pronounced it
No Ecobox referral even though the customer confirmed she is packing all her own boxes
top_strength: He proactively revised the estimate DOWN — the quote on file assumed a fully furnished two-bedroom at 5.5 hours, and after learning she was discarding the bedroom set and taking mostly boxes he cut it to 4 hours and explained he was still padding it conservatively 'to set your budget up for success.' He also caught the dumpster run as the likely time sink and asked how far it was from the unit.
coaching_note: Hector left roughly 20 points on the table by skipping two entire pitches he had a natural opening for. When the customer asked 'do I still have to go on the website and finish all the steps?', he answered with Meet Your Mover and the day-before text but never mentioned No Worries Damage Coverage or the On-Time Guarantee — on a move where she is boxing her own belongings and going up to a 4th floor, the $2,000 coverage is the exact reassurance she needed. Bigger still: the Save Your Ass prep speech was never delivered on a move he himself estimated at 4 hours, where consolidating drawers and taking a carload would have directly cut her bill. Fix the front of the call too — open with the agenda statement and a 'sound good?', and ask about the elevator and box count before quoting, because a 4th-floor walk-up would blow the 4-hour estimate apart.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and affirming ('awesome', 'fantastic', 'appreciate your flexibility'), accommodated the date change without friction, and made a genuine rapport moment complimenting her name — held back from a 5 only by never using her name and a rambling, hard-to-follow explanation of afternoon start windows that forced her to ask 'so 4:30 is not gonna work?'
